findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `status` enum (running|passed|failed|attaching|unknown) in the new gate_run schema (or $ref a common $def), matching the live GateRunOut/gate_status vocabulary.
evidence: Plan declares gate_run with 'job_id, status' required but no enum for status.

Live vocabulary is running|passed|failed|attaching|unknown — GateRunOut docstring (_mcp_models.py:468-469) and gate_status tool docstring (_mcp_reads.py:203-206: 'Status is running, then passed or failed; ... attaching awaits ... unknown marks an unrecognized ID').

The gate_status tool prose gates consumer behavior on this value ('Read plan findings only after findings.readable is true'), so the vocabulary is a load-bearing decision rule for an LLM/agent client.
Repo convention enumerates such discriminators: gate_output.schema.json verdict enum [pass,fail]; ticket_state pin_status/phase_status enums.
findings.finding: The new gate_run output schema declares a required `status` field but never defines its value vocabulary, even though the field is the agent's polling-state discriminator with a known closed set.

scenarios: An MCP agent polling gate_status cannot rely on the advertised outputSchema to know the terminal vs non-terminal status values, since any string validates.
findings.suggested_fix: In gate_run.schema.json declare status as {"type":"string","enum":["running","passed","failed","attaching","unknown"]}, mirroring the gate_status tool docstring.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the back-out mechanism for the stricter outputSchema cutover (e.g. revert of install_canonical_output_schemas restores pass-through behavior) and confirm the wire-validation ACs cover every schema-bearing tool, not only show_ticket / ready_tickets / write_ack.
evidence: 'The MCP SDK validates every structured result against the advertised outputSchema (jsonschema.validate(...))'
'FastMCP's output_model is a pass-through RootModel' — i.e. no strict validation existed before
release-notes AC documents the null->absent change but no back-out/rollback mechanism is described
findings.finding: The change flips the MCP wire contract from a pass-through RootModel (no validation) to a strict advertised outputSchema that the SDK validates and can REJECT, and also drops null-valued keys to absent. The destructiveness is acknowledged (release-notes AC lists null->absent fields) but no rollback / back-out path or expand-contract sequencing is stated for the client-facing contract change — if a live payload for one of the 32 schema-bearing tools violates its canonical schema at runtime, the SDK will raise where it previously passed.
scenarios: A tool payload the wire tests did not cover emits a key or type the canonical schema forbids; the SDK raises at request time with no fallback and no documented way to revert the stricter validation quickly
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence noting that reverting install_canonical_output_schemas restores the pass-through RootModel (clean rollback), and add wire-payload validation cases (or an existing-session parametrization) covering transition_ticket/reopen_ticket, gate_status, attach_commits, and verify_completion_status so no schema-bearing tool is advertised strict without a payload that proves it validates.
